findings.reason: A finite colored crystal decomposes into a branching six-vertex component and a three-vertex chain. The original two standalone screenshots contain only a dense arrow enumeration. Displaying that exact graph materially clarifies component membership, the two highest vertices, and the 6+3 split; warranted under the expanded explanatory-diagram scope, although the original proof is complete.

correction: Added only a final Remarks illustration of the nine tensor-crystal vertices and eight nonzero lowering arrows. The original carrier is an unchanged byte prefix; all frontmatter, claims, hypotheses, dependencies, sources, publication status and proof remain unchanged.

diagram_math_checks.result: Vertices (j,k) are exactly u_j tensor u_k for j,k in {1,2,3}; colored edge i is the partial lowering map f_i from B(lambda_1) tensor B(lambda_1) to that crystal union {0}, restricted to nonzero images. Reverse existing edges are e_i by def-crystal-graph-epsilon-phi-and-weight Definition/F1. The two-case convention is def-tensor-product-of-crystals (ii): act first iff phi_i(u_j)>epsilon_i(u_k), otherwise second.

Independently enumerated all 18 vertex/color pairs using epsilon(1)=(0,0), epsilon(2)=(1,0), epsilon(3)=(0,1), phi(1)=(1,0), phi(2)=(0,1), phi(3)=(0,0), and standard arrows f_1(1)=2, f_2(2)=3. Exactly these eight nonzero results occur: 11 -1-> 21; 21 -1-> 22; 21 -2-> 31; 22 -2-> 32; 31 -1-> 32; 32 -2-> 33; 12 -2-> 13; 13 -1-> 23. They agree with verification step 3.1 and the eight explicit TikZ segments. All other selected-factor images are zero.

The left connected component has six distinct vertices {11,21,22,31,32,33} and six edges; the right has {12,13,23} and two edges. All nine pairs occur once, with no edge between components. Indegrees in left order are (0,1,1,1,2,1), outdegrees (1,2,1,1,1,0); right indegrees (0,1,1), outdegrees (1,1,0). Highest vertices 11 and 12 have weights 2lambda_1 and lambda_2 by Example and step 2.1; thm-highest-weight-components-in-a-tensor-product-crystal(b), as used in step 3.1, gives the displayed component labels. Every i-arrow changes one standard factor along its i-arrow, so total weight decreases by alpha_i.

The entire existing Verification, including exhaustive arrow enumeration in step 3.1, is byte-identical. The new caption states that the verification establishes all arrows and identifications independently of the illustration.
